key_insight: Wat3R shows that 3D scene geometry can be learned for underwater environments without requiring expensive underwater 3D annotations. It adapts a feed-forward reconstruction model trained in air to underwater scenes using semi-supervised cross-domain learning.
problem_solved: Underwater 3D reconstruction is hard because light attenuation and scattering degrade image quality, and large-scale accurate 3D labels are not available. Existing methods often depend on dense annotations that are impractical in real underwater settings.
method: Uses a cross-domain semi-supervised framework to transfer knowledge from air-domain 3D reconstruction to underwater scenes.
Leverages unlabeled or weakly labeled underwater data to reduce dependence on manual 3D annotations.
Adapts a feed-forward 3D reconstruction model so it can generalize across domains with different visual properties.
impact: This matters because it makes underwater 3D perception more practical and scalable, especially where labeled data is scarce or impossible to collect. It can help deploy AI systems for marine robotics, inspection, and environmental monitoring with less annotation cost.
